principle.name: Accessibility First
principle.description: Design for all users from the start, ensuring WCAG 2.1 AA compliance
principle.rationale: Accessibility is not optional - it's essential for inclusive design and legal compliance

example.good: Use semantic HTML, proper labels, sufficient color contrast, and keyboard navigation
example.bad: Rely on color alone for status indicators, skip alt text, ignore keyboard users

principle.name: Mobile-First Responsive Design
principle.description: Design for mobile devices first, then scale up to larger screens
principle.rationale: Mobile traffic dominates web usage; mobile-first ensures better performance and UX

example.good: Single column on mobile, progressive enhancement for tablets and desktop
example.bad: Desktop layout that breaks or requires excessive zooming on mobile

principle.name: Consistency Over Creativity
principle.description: Maintain design consistency across all components and interactions
principle.rationale: Consistency reduces cognitive load and improves user confidence

example.good: All buttons follow same visual style, hover states, and interaction patterns
example.bad: Different button styles for similar actions throughout the interface

principle.name: Visual Hierarchy
principle.description: Guide user attention through strategic use of size, color, and spacing

guidelines.guideline: Use size to indicate importance (larger = more important)
Apply color purposefully for meaning and brand consistency
Use white space to reduce clutter and improve focus
Establish clear reading patterns (F-pattern, Z-pattern)

principle.name: Color and Typography
principle.description: Use color and typography strategically for readability and brand

guidelines.guideline: Ensure 4.5:1 contrast ratio for normal text (WCAG AA)
Limit color palette to 3-5 primary colors plus neutrals
Use no more than 2-3 font families for consistency
Establish clear type scale (h1-h6, body, small, etc.)

principle.name: Feedback and Affordance
principle.description: Provide clear feedback for all interactions and make actions discoverable

guidelines.guideline: Show hover states for all interactive elements
Provide loading indicators for async operations
Use micro-interactions to acknowledge user actions
Make disabled states clearly distinguishable

principle.name: Progressive Disclosure
principle.description: Reveal complexity gradually to avoid overwhelming users

guidelines.guideline: Hide advanced features behind clear entry points
Use tooltips and help text strategically
Group related information logically
Allow users to control detail level

principle.name: Performance-Aware Design
principle.description: Design with performance constraints in mind

guidelines.guideline: Optimize images and assets for web delivery
Minimize custom fonts and font weights
Use CSS animations instead of JavaScript when possible
Design for graceful degradation on slow connections

pitfall.description: Over-designing with excessive animations and effects
pitfall.why_problematic: Slows performance, distracts users, can cause motion sickness
pitfall.correct_approach: Use animations purposefully to enhance understanding and delight

pitfall.why_problematic: Expensive to retrofit, may require complete redesign
pitfall.correct_approach: Design accessibility from the start, test with assistive technologies

pitfall.description: Designing in isolation from development constraints
pitfall.why_problematic: Creates unrealistic expectations and implementation challenges
pitfall.correct_approach: Collaborate with developers throughout the design process

category.name: accessibility
category.item: All interactive elements are keyboard accessible
Color contrast meets WCAG AA standards
Forms have proper labels and error messages
Focus indicators are visible and clear

category.name: responsiveness
category.item: Text remains readable at all sizes

category.name: usability
category.item: Feedback is provided for all actions
Error states are clear and helpful
